# The OpenTimestamps client and its full dependency closure, every one pinned
# by version and wheel hash (audit SC-2). The timestamp, OTS upgrade and
# release-asset jobs install it with --require-hashes --no-deps
# --only-binary :all:, so pip takes exactly these wheels or fails, and runs
# no package build code. Hashes are PyPI's published sha256 digests,
# cross-checked against the downloaded wheels. The pycryptodomex wheel is the
# manylinux x86_64 build the ubuntu-latest runners take; it is cp37-abi3, so
# a newer runner Python still takes it, but a different architecture (arm64)
# selects another wheel and the install fails closed. Re-pin then by adding
# that wheel's published hash to the pycryptodomex entry.
opentimestamps-client==0.7.2 \
    --hash=sha256:84e604d7f76534da4bab61ab62b211a6559aa988da51438408ae7947b0e8b7ba
opentimestamps==0.4.5 \
    --hash=sha256:a4912b3bd1b612a3ef5fac925b9137889e6c5cb91cc9e76c8202a2bf8abe26b5
python-bitcoinlib==0.12.2 \
    --hash=sha256:2f29a9f475f21c12169b3a6cc8820f34f11362d7ff1200a5703dce3e4e903a44
appdirs==1.4.4 \
    --hash=sha256:a841dacd6b99318a741b166adb07e19ee71a274450e68237b4650ca1055ab128
GitPython==3.2.0 \
    --hash=sha256:bd70c5ec05cd2b797423e7eb312147d2458d3cca92085888fba2213f85905537
